note: Saved formal results, scoped to each modeled or historical version. Result categories do not certify current repair release readiness. Source mapping and omissions are in each linked note.

rows.what: Within the modeled QF_UF fragment, the original rejects every witness for the published satisfiable scope-conflict pattern. The repaired model is sound and complete for ground-key witnesses under its coverage hypotheses.
rows.limit: One sort, one unary function, let, =, not and and. No whole-evaluator soundness proof; implementation correspondence is argued and differentially tested, not machine-proved.

rows.what: With the original checksum a run always keeps its first valid submission (under the task's highest-pass-rate-first rule); with the fixed one it keeps the highest-scoring valid submission. Checked over 5.4 million states, and against the real selection code on 112,944 runs.
rows.limit: Runs of up to four submissions and three score values

rows.what: The repaired flip rule matches strict convexity for one modeled flip and rejects the demonstrated folding flip. The proof does not cover the meshes; full convex-hull coverage of the 13 regenerated v2.2 inputs is checked by an exact-arithmetic census, not in Lean.
rows.limit: One flip, not the whole mesh. Hull coverage (13 of 13 v2.2 files; v2.1 left gaps in 12) and CPU behavior checked by exact scripts and runs.

rows.what: The modeled original cost excludes the last target; the repaired model counts the whole cost. Verdicts differ only in the resulting over-limit window.
rows.limit: Per-state sizes taken as given; does not prove attainment of the 9.67-point official-corpus upper bound.

rows.what: The fixed grader never scores an assessment that leaves out a rule, gives exactly the original total for every assessment it accepts, and never gives full marks to a rule whose row records a deduction. The proof found three gaps in the first version of this fix and a probe of the real code found a fourth; the fix was then revised. The model is of v2.1 (`87f0e340…`), not the current v2.2 (`a0af4360…`).
rows.limit: Models v2.1 only; v2.2's JSON block selection and reading of decimal-string rule scores are not modelled. Text fields reduced to yes/no; deductive rules only (all 12 here); the proof starts from an already-parsed assessment

rows.what: The first fixed grader (v2, `32caddb1…`) accepts a file exactly when every test node has one integer class, and then scores it as the original does. The current v2.1 (`7b4860ec…`), which matches keys by `str()` and rejects `str()` key collisions, is not modelled: it scores integer-keyed files that the original scores 0. A general lemma shows that keeping the best submission can turn added variance into expected gain; no gain for a real solver was shown.
rows.limit: Models the first fix (v2, `32caddb1…`) only; v2.1's `str()` key handling and duplicate-key rejection are not covered. Four ASCII control characters behave differently in Python; the size check is not modelled

rows.what: The historical v2 score model limits credit from failed or unverified workloads and preserves the formula when all verify. It models the validation flag, not whether every timed output was actually inspected. It does not verify the current v2.2 repair.
rows.limit: Historical v2 abstraction; real arithmetic rather than IEEE doubles; quality is a Boolean. Current v2.2 native scorer controls passed, but the saved proof does not cover that revision; full source-build eval_cmd integration remains unverified.

rows.what: The historical model checks calendar validity, matching weekday and time over years 1–9999, and its weekday arithmetic agrees with Python. That modeled domain admits years forbidden by the cited HTTP-date standard; this is not proof of the current year≥1900 v2.1 repair.
rows.limit: Hand-written parser; historical relaxed year domain, not standards conformance. Current v2.1 native paired eval_cmd controls passed; a proof for the revised domain and whole-task certification are not established.

rows.what: The model proves the 40% comparison after FX conversion using gross exposure as denominator, and a conditional monotonicity result. This repairs currency arithmetic but does not implement the policy denominator of fund NAV.
rows.limit: Historical FX/gross-exposure model only: it does not prove the current v2.1 NAV denominator or full-grader integration. Current helper controls cover both score directions.

rows.what: No submission can score above 320 raw; the fixed scale maps the starter's documented score to 0 and that maximum to 100. The regraded real submission's 160.76 and 50.08 are exact. The fix's main change, measuring the starter in the same run, is not modelled.
rows.limit: Scale arithmetic only; timing noise is outside the model

rows.what: Two installed statements are refuted against the task definitions; both corrected statements are proved.
rows.limit: Does not validate helper filtering or release integration: paired Mathlib 491a409 differs from actual eval_cmd baseline 3203991; final grader/work images unverified.

rows.what: The original library computes v *= v wrongly; the fixed library is correct whether or not the operands are the same object.
rows.limit: Arithmetic modulo 4 instead of 2¹⁶

rows.what: For axis-aligned rectangles, a closed-form version of the fixed criterion rejects exactly the pairs whose interiors overlap beyond its 1e-6 tolerance. The modelled slab algorithm matches it on every published witness and on all 441 placements of two squares.
rows.limit: The algorithm itself is checked only on those cases; general polygons, rotations and strip bounds are not covered

rows.what: The original correctness check depends only on overall money balance and final order books, so it cannot detect a fee swap or dropped messages that leave the final books unchanged (as observed in all 50 rounds).
rows.limit: Unchanged final books is observed, not proved; the fix relies on the project's own tests, which cannot be proved here

rows.what: Each case scores at most 2N². The total bound 92,304 maps to 2543510/121003 under the original scale. The formulas establish conditional per-score conversions, not exact conversion of all published leaderboard averages.
rows.limit: 92,304 is an upper bound, not a demonstrated attainable total. Averaging across clipping or piecewise boundaries invalidates conversion from an aggregate alone.

rows.what: The fixed scale and every converted leaderboard value follow exactly from the published (one-decimal) scores.
rows.limit: Only the change of scale; the physics convention is not formalizable

rows.what: Every valid answer in the tester model totals at least 712.538, implying the stated score ceiling. The arithmetic 5×30=150 supports the per-input budget correction.
rows.limit: Tester model checked against 294 strings; no proof of CPU policy or harness result collection. Required wait-overlay end-to-end integration pending.

rows.what: 992 game days need about 1,658 seconds at the model rate and 1,661 to 1,705 seconds at the measured rates, against a 120-second budget per scenario.
rows.limit: Arithmetic only

rows.what: Every published score change is exact, and fully passed or fully failed test groups score the same in both versions.
rows.limit: The identity test itself is not formalized

rows.what: Given the observed behaviour of the starter (one value class in 12 of 12 runs), the original body-suppression test can never fail; every published score change is exact.
rows.limit: The report-format test depends on an XML parser

rows.what: In any run with at least one other submission, a compile failure can never change any score out of 100.
rows.limit: Exact rationals in place of floating point; harness filters not modelled

rows.what: A zero-hit answer is wrong on 37 of the 50 official puzzles, each by a certificate the tester cannot satisfy.
rows.limit: The other 13 large puzzles would need a SAT-scale refutation; the CPU-count fix is not formalized (checked by runs)

rows.what: The misplaced reference point gives a do-nothing solution exactly 2.84005 points, and never adds more.
rows.limit: Per-case scores taken from the saved log

rows.what: Every score lies between 0 and 30; 30 is the formula's maximum (both mean rewards ≥ 300), not shown to be reachable by a policy.
rows.limit: Simulation not modelled

rows.what: Under the stated real-power domain hypotheses, for a fixed benchmark the two excess-return formulas preserve sign and order. This is neither a proof of whole-score ordering nor of a universal score-change bound.
rows.limit: The +0.3921/−0.10 envelope is a restricted numerical sensitivity sweep, not a universal bound; implementation correspondence is a source argument.

rows.what: The original test-credit rule can count an unrelated failure as a pass; the fixed version's rule cannot. This is one of the four fixed defects; hidden-test placement, Cargo stopping at a failing test file and the missing vendored files are settled by paired runs, not by the model.
rows.limit: Up to four tests and one or two exempt tests per package; requires the expected test count to be at least the number of tests run; one test binary only
